shape: two people in an ordinary moment; one finally says the thing they never said

slides.text: you handed me the dry tea towel without looking up from the roasting pan.
you always took the wash basin, telling me i was too clumsy with the hot tap.
so for ten years i stood by the drainer, complaining about every greasy fork.
but tonight you stayed at the sink while the water went cold around your wrists.
you said you only took the wash side so the boiling water would never burn my hands.
i dried the last chipped mug three times, [[just so i didn't have to leave the room]].

caption:
you took the rougher half of every chore and made it sound like an insult so i wouldn't notice.
send this to the brother or sister who always took the hot water first.

#siblings #siblinglove #growingupwithsiblings #oldersiblings
alt: A short story about an older sibling who always insisted on washing the dishes so their younger sibling would never get burned by the hot water.
hook_options: you handed me the dry tea towel without looking up from the roasting pan.
we were standing at the kitchen sink at ten, splitting the dinner plates.
you pushed the dry tea towel into my ribs and turned the hot tap all the way on.
